inputs.root_cause: ORA-VALIDATE-001's obligation requires validate() to 'distinguish errors from interoperability warnings', but every Diagnostic this package ever emitted used Severity.ERROR -- Severity.WARNING, already supported by the shared Diagnostic/Severity type, was never constructed anywhere in lifecycle.py.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 6 new tests prove a genuine, honest interoperability-warning finding: a document whose declared version is older than what its own features require now gets a Severity.WARNING diagnostic from validate(), while ValidationReport.is_valid correctly stays True -- reusing load()'s existing declared_version/detected_version drift-detection machinery, previously exposed as data only, never diagnosed.
inputs.regression_tier: full ora package suite (tests/python/ora) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Read lifecycle.py's validate() and load() in full: load() already computes declared_version (document.version, unconstrained by the spec's own grammar) and detected_version (via _detect_version(), inferring the minimum profile actually used) but only returns both as OraImage fields -- never diagnoses their disagreement. validate() never even computes detected_version.

2. Confirmed via an interactive probe that validate() currently reports zero diagnostics for a document declaring 0.0.1 while using an isolation feature that requires 0.0.4 -- a real, previously undiagnosed drift.

3. Read the shared Diagnostic/Severity/ValidationReport type (format_factory.core.diagnostics): confirmed ValidationReport.is_valid deliberately excludes Severity.WARNING from invalidating a report -- exactly the distinction this obligation asks for, already built, just never used by ora.

4. Added _parse_profile_version() (a narrow x.y.z regex parser, since declared_version has no format constraint in the spec's own grammar and can be any string) and _version_drift_diagnostics(), returning a Severity.WARNING Diagnostic only when both versions parse and declared < detected -- an unparseable declared version means 'cannot determine', not 'assume the worst', and must never raise.
5. Wired the new check into validate() alongside the existing baseline-asset and layer-PNG diagnostics.
6. Re-ran the interactive probe across 4 cases (drift present, no drift, unparseable declared version, declared ahead of detected) -- all 4 behaved correctly on the first attempt.

7. Wrote 6 tests: the warning fires with the correct message content, the warning does not flip is_valid, no warning when versions already match, no warning when declared is ahead of detected, an unparseable declared version produces neither a warning nor a crash, and a warning coexists with a genuine ERROR in the same report (aggregation still holds, severities remain distinguishable).

8. Ran ruff (clean) on lifecycle.py and the new test file. Ran the full ora suite (311 passed, was 305, +6) and the full 6-format regression (3113 passed, was 3107, +6; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

9. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-0982177c8dff4ec4, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3113 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3107 passed

evidence.oracle: SELF-CONSISTENT format_factory-only evidence per the execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule, not cross-checked against a reference OpenRaster implementation.
evidence.obligations_moved_breakdown: 1 obligation (SAL-ORA-OBL-F2672F4CCD923AC2, ORA-VALIDATE-001) promoted partial->implemented: the 'distinguish errors from interoperability warnings' clause is now proven with a genuine finding, reusing existing drift-detection data that was previously computed but never diagnosed. The obligation's other three clauses (per-layer independent validation, stable aggregation, no repair-unless-requested) were already proven by prior evidence and remain unchanged.
